reasons: Rule expects a Vendor indemnity; the cited Section 7 contains only liability caps, a consequential-damages waiver and an attorneys'-fees waiver, with 'indemnification' appearing solely in the heading — no operative indemnity of any kind, which is walk-away territory (no Vendor IP indemnity) and correctly classified as 'missing'.
The bare non-infringement warranty in Section 5(c) is a warranty only, with no defence/indemnity obligation, so it does not satisfy the rule; the detection guidance is properly applied.

Inserted Section 7(d) tracks the model language closely (IP infringement, breach of law, unauthorised access to Company data/Confidential Information, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) and adds standard notice, control and cooperation mechanics — reaching the preferred position.

Placement is appropriate (immediately after the limitation-of-liability subsections, as the redline guidance directs) and the heading conforming edit removes the misleading one-sided 'OF CONTRACTOR' reference; changed-character ratio on p0034 is low and the insertion is otherwise additive.

The reciprocal Company indemnity is narrowed exactly as the playbook prescribes (Company-furnished materials and Company's breach of law), so it does not gratuitously expand our client's exposure; the carve-out from the 7(a) cap is justified for a newly inserted indemnity and the comment properly offers the 3x super-cap fallback.
Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice, cites the playbook position and does not misstate the contract; severity 'critical' matches the rule.
